The short version for Clearing homeowners

1960s housing is the normal case in Clearing. Masonry walls, wood trim, and most of that wood somewhere you need a ladder to reach. Which puts most of the cost in reach and in preparation. Painting a Clearing house is not a wall-area job, it is a trim and access job.

interior painting, exterior painting, cabinet refinishing and the making-good that comes first: that is the list in Clearing. The shop is 3.2 straight-line miles away at 7900 W. 83rd St. in Bridgeview.

The short answers

  • Can we do your job? Almost certainly. In Clearing it is interior painting and exterior painting most weeks, plus the drywall, plaster and carpentry that goes underneath both.
  • What will it cost? There is no price list on this site, because there is no honest local one to publish yet. Every job is quoted after we walk it. What moves the number on a Clearing house is the condition of the trim rather than the size of the house, because in Clearing it is the wood that has been weathering and the masonry that has not.
  • What usually needs doing first? The wood above the masonry. On Clearing houses the walls outlast the trim by a long way, so the trim is the job and the brick is not.
  • When can you come? We are 3.2 straight-line miles out, and travel is not a hidden line on a quote from us. Sooner than the size of the job would suggest. Nothing about the drive to Clearing has to be scheduled around, so small work gets seen rather than deferred.

How soon can we get to Clearing?

The shop is at 7900 W. 83rd St. in Bridgeview, 3.2 straight-line miles from Clearing. The south and southwest sides are the city work this business actually does, and that stock is the same brick and plaster as the inner suburbs, so it is the same job rather than a different one.

For scale, the nearest other place on this site is Bedford Park, 0.8 miles from Clearing, and Clearing sits in Cook County.

The whole city is not on offer and there is no point pretending otherwise. Chicago is too big and too well covered for one small shop to claim all of it, so anything well north of here gets an early no rather than a late one.

The parts of a Clearing quote that actually move

Interiors from around 1960 run to lower ceilings and more doors than a modern plan, and Clearing averages 5.8 rooms a unit. Six-panel doors, full baseboard runs and heavy casing: trim is where an interior job gets long. It is also the line most quotes leave vague, so ask for it on its own. 6,618 households own in Clearing and 2,405 rent, which produces two different phone calls. One wants the house to look right for ten years. The other wants a unit clean and let by the first of the month. Both are real work and neither should be quoted like the other.

What an estimate here has to account for

  • Containment, not just paint. 73 percent of housing in Clearing was built before 1970, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.
  • Distance, stated. Clearing is 3.2 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Clearing is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is brick and brick-and-frame ranch and split-level. Exterior work in Clearing is fascia, soffit, gable ends and window trim, most of it off a ladder rather than off the ground.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1960 median build year, and the split between 57.4 percent detached houses, 8 percent attached homes and 34.1 percent in buildings of two units or more.

Inference, and worth saying so. Wall material in Clearing is not in the Census tables or the regional data, which is why that sentence carries no number when everything else here does.

Is there lead paint in my house?

Old paint is the thing to know about here. Clearing is largely 1960s housing, and anything painted before 1978 may have lead in the layers underneath. It is handled rather than avoided: the room is closed off, the dust is contained while the work happens, and the site is cleaned to a set standard before anyone leaves.

In practice the rule is about containment and cleanup rather than about paint. In a Clearing room it sets a threshold of roughly six square feet of disturbed interior paint, twenty square feet outside, and any window replacement or demolition is covered whatever the area. Sanding the casing on one 1960-median window clears that in a few minutes.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Clearing.

Read 73 percent built before 1970 as the lower bound it is. The community-area data carries no 1978 bucket at all, so the share that actually matters is larger than the published one in Clearing. The federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule applies to work that disturbs paint in housing built before 1978, and in Illinois the EPA administers it directly rather than through a state program.

In Clearing it is worth asking about before the work starts rather than after the sanding has. Ask whoever you hire to say, in plain terms, how they intend to handle it at your particular address.

This site does not claim EPA lead-safe firm certification. No number has been supplied, so the trust panel below shows it as pending. Ask for it directly, from anyone quoting work in Clearing.

Of the 9,412 housing units in Clearing, 73 percent were built before 1970 and 9.5 percent before 1940, against a median build year of 1960. This is old-city housing, and it behaves like it: plaster, deep casing and a lot of coats already on the woodwork.

The tenure split is 6,618 owner households against 2,405 renting, or 73.3 percent owner occupied. Structure follows it: 57.4 percent detached houses, 8 percent townhomes and rowhouses, 34.1 percent in buildings of two or more. At 5.8 rooms a unit, that is the trim footage an interior quote is really made of. Median home value is $303,890.

Against the other 22 Chicago community areas covered here, Clearing sits in the top four for the newest housing by median build year (1960, first of them all), the largest townhome and rowhouse share (8 percent) and the smallest share built before 1970 (73 percent).

Where Clearing departs most from the 76 place average: prewar housing at 9.5 percent against a 15.8 percent average, housing built before 1970 at 73 percent against a 56.9 percent average and housing in buildings of two or more at 34.1 percent against a 29 percent average.

Source: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, Community Data Snapshots 2026, drawing on American Community Survey 2024 estimates. Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

Questions

Asked about Clearing

What changes the price most on a house here?

Prep. Housing here runs to a 1960 median, which means several coats are already on the woodwork and some of them were put on badly. Undoing that is the expensive part, and it is the part that a fast number leaves out and a slow one explains.

Why do these figures cover the community area rather than my ZIP code?

Because ZIP codes cut through neighborhood lines and community areas do not. One ZIP on the southwest side covers three different neighborhoods with three different kinds of housing, so a page built on it would be describing an average of places that have nothing to do with each other. The 9,412 housing units counted here are the ones inside Clearing, and the source is named at the bottom of the page.

How quickly can somebody look at it?

Clearing is 3.2 straight-line miles from the shop, which is close enough that looking at the work and doing the work do not have to be the same trip. That matters most on small jobs, because a repair that is worth doing gets seen instead of being pushed into a bigger job later. Call 708-935-4289.

Is the $303,890 median home value in Clearing what a job here costs?

No, and the two are unrelated. $303,890 is the Census estimate of what homes in Clearing are worth, and it is on this page because the age and the size of the housing describe the work. No price for painting or remodeling appears anywhere on this site, because no local range has been established that would survive being checked. Every job is quoted after we stand in it.
